line.text: '* Avoid deploying any unnecessary Jump Beacons. On the higher difficulty levels, their maintenance cost is very high.'
'* The "Dry Dock" perk lowers maintenance of docked Capital ships by 75% and smaller ships by 25%.'
'* Ship Quality directly affects maintenance costs. It can nearly double for the lowest quality ships!'
'* "Advanced ships" are 35% more expensive to maintain.'
'* Ships you build that are not of your own Race are higher in maintenance costs.'
'* For ships produced at outposts having the perk "Advanced engineering", maintenance costs will be cut by 50%.'
'* Yaki ship maintenance is 25% less while you have infamy.'
'* Build your own Advanced Satellite Factory and base some fast M5 fighters to it. You can then set them as Automated explorers. This works from outposts also.'
'* Automated explorers have a 15 jump range from their home base.'
'* Explorers based at the same station will always explore different sectors without overlap.'
'* Good to Know: A.I. explorers on hard difficulty level have the ability to claim sectors.'
'* Explorers will avoid Blacklisted sectors. You may have to explore those personally.'
'* On Hard difficulty, the other nations will periodically "clean out" some of your satellites, so your automated explorers will stay very busy replacing them.'

'* Capital ships do not do very well at docking or traversing through gates when you are in-system with them. They tend to clog up because of their collision avoidance which is active only when you are present in the system. If you want them to move without clogging up, be somewhere else. For moving around within the system, they do ok with you there.'

'* If you are In System with your fleet, all damage (from all sides) is magnified greatly, so if you want a fight over quickly, be there in that system. Out of system, all damages are reduced to about 1/3.'

'* Chaff is not considered for OOS battles, so if youre never where the fighting is, dont bother with it. OOS battles are simulated and use a simplified calculation which doesnt consider all factors.'
'* Upgrade your larger ships in the outpost Hangar, using colored crystals. In particular, the CCDS1/2/3 will allow Chaff to be used to repel the 3 missile types in the game.'

'* The jump station perk is limited to 4 in the galaxy, so use it in critical areas where you may get attacked and cant risk relying on fragile jump beacons. Losing your jump beacon when trying to respond to an attack will ruin your day.'

'* Remember you cannot place beacons in sectors you do not own on hard difficulty. This makes expansion far more difficult and mirrors the A.I. limitations. The only means to expand is to use a TL or large Capital ship to move and drop a factory or outpost somewhere and then you can place a beacon.'

'* The A.I. will sometimes send in small Raiding strikes deep into your territory during war time. These are small fleets of fast fighters that will kill your outpost agents and traders, so protect the homeland.'
'* The "Faster research" Perk can greatly improve any research in that sector.'
'* Researching ships of your own Race gives a large bonus.'
'* Researching ships of a type matching nations that border that sector gives you a bonus.'
'* A Research Favor from another race can improve your research rate temporarily.'
'* If you are in a Coalition, this can improve your research rate.'
'* OCV ship research is improved in systems that have higher OCV signals.'
'* Yaki ship research is improved if you have Infamy.'
'* Terran ships can be researched only in systems that have Terran Memory.'
'* You can use your data scanner to scan your own ships that you do not have a blueprint of.'

'* If you cannot catch someone, you cannot kill them. Speed kills. The Split have the fastest ships, but they are somewhat weak in defenses. Used properly, they can be deadly. Each race has their own particular advantages to learn and take advantage of.'
'* Escort your large Capital ships with some M6s. These provide good anti-fighter defense and they can hold up in a heavy fight.'

'* Create fast Raiding fleets of M3s and using the Fleet settings screen, set them to attack only Haulers and then set them to patrol an Enemy factions space. They will quickly decimate enemy haulers while running from other fights. This can devastate the economy of an opponent.'

'* Missiles in Renegades have greatly enhanced damage. They are expensive, but much more damaging than in any prior versions of X3 mods. M7Ms are very effective long range anti-capital forces, and M8s can be devastating against fighters.'

'* Grouping your forces is essential to surviving large engagements. Streaming in your attack ships 1 by 1 is the best way to lose them. When invading a sector, consider first sending in one or two fast fighters and directing them to the far side of the target system. When the defenses move far from your gate to engage those fighters, stream in your large ships.'

'* For large capital ship engagements In-System, use fast nimble fighters to draw fire from enemy capital ships and away from your capital ships. These force the enemy to waste their high-damage weapons on nimble hard-to-hit ships.'
'* Be sure to setup a Supplier in the Fleet Settings screen to automatically restore your missile reserves.'
'* Moving Capital ships through gates is vastly slower with the player In-System. If you need to get them through a gate fast, be somewhere else.'

'* In systems where you have no jump beacon, use ONLY your local logistics agents to import/export everything from/to the local factories and then set other logistics agents to move FULL loads between other outposts. This maximizes the inter-sector Loads you carry and is the KEY to efficiency.'

'* Setup correctly, In most system, you should only need 2 Logistics agents to service all the factories there. For large systems holding 15 factories, you might need 3 agents max, but more is a waste.'

'* Outpost Trade agents are used for buying materals from NPCs or selling excess items to NPCs. When neither is needed, they start Trading between NPCs for pure profit, so they can be a huge source of income over time. Also remember that any successful trade to an NPC raises your standings with them and that can be a game changer.'
'* If you can afford the maintenance costs, research a FAST TS class ship to use as your logistics agents. The faster resources are moved around your empire, the smoother it will run. '
'* If you find your outpost agents doing nothing most of the time, assign them to do something else. Optimize the use of your agents to keep costs down.'

'* Review the "Logistics" screen in your personal console. This summarizes the total empire production and consumption, showing you exactly when you need more or less factories. It is critical to review when you get a larger empire.'

'* The default station trade range in Mayhem 3 is 8 jumps (does not include jump beacons). Your agents will limit themselves to this range. If you raise it, the demand on your CPU can rise dramatically, so keep an eye out for this.'

'* Your logistics ships will need maintenance once in a while. Be sure to review your Maintenance screen in your Personal console and send them for Inspection occasionally. Otherwise their maintenance will be very high.'

'* The Truelight Seeker is a souped-up repair ship! Target a friendly and shoot, or use the *Repair command* from the special commands and it will carry out the task automatically. It has 6 repair lasers and can repair large ships in the field.'
'* Do not undervalue Mining ships. While mining ore and silicon, they also bring in colored Crystals which are good for ship upgrades and valuable resources to sell at trade stations.'
'* When at war, consider placing a few picket ships out 2 or 3 jumps from your main Hubs. This can be an essential early warning system if you get too busy micromanaging.'
'* The chances that the A.I. will declare war on you go up if you have Infamy, a bad reputation with them, hold a Dejure sector, or if you have a low "Total Ship Power to System Count ratio".'

'* On hard difficulty and fighting far from home, consider loading a cheap factory and a Jump Beacon on one of your Capital ships, assuming you have one with the necessary cargo space. In a pinch, you can run to an unclaimed sector, deploy the station and then drop the Jump Beacon, allowing you to escape.'

line.text: '* Generally, the A.I. must share a border with you in order to declare war on you.'

'* Depending on how much progress you have towards a ship blueprint, recycling a ship will give anywhere between 10-40% of its blueprint, up until 85% (50% for advanced ships). The remaining 15% must be completed by research or via the data scanner.'

'* Different races have different ship advantages and loadouts. The Split have the fastest ships, Teladi have largest cargo bays, Boron have Ion weapon, Terran have most powerful weapons. Each races has their own disadvantages as well.'
'* Renegade ships move faster when they start fleeing to a station.'
'* Fleet members can get dispersed during combat operations. You can peridiodically regroup by issuing the "Followers: Join with Commander" command.'

'* If you want your fleets to focus their fire on one target at a time, set their Scanning Range to 0 km, and set "Followers engage commanders target" to YES. It can be less efficient, but you will lose fewer ships'

'* You can assign an automated Missile Supplier that will top up all your ships in the field. Upgrade a TS hauler with a Transporter Device and position it out in space. In the Fleet Settings screen, select "Supplier:" and choose this hauler.'

'* Suppliers will either retrieve missiles from its homebase, or build more there as needed and automatically stock up your ships. Set your ship restock amounts at the bottom of the "Advanced/Weapons.." menu for that ship.'
'* This screen shows the slowest ship in the fleet. This is important because a fleet travels at the pace of its slowest member.'
'* For fast raiding fleets composed of fighters, it is useful to select the option to "Ignore Big and Huge Ships".'
'* Fleets can automatically reinforce themselves by setting the "Build Followers" menu. This is limited to only one type of ship, but it can be useful for homogeneous fleets.'
'* Port research takes time and money. A higher research rate will improve your port research time.'
'* Oxygen and accounting hacks take the longest to complete.'
'* The "hacking station" perk is required to convert a research station into a hacking station.'
'* Good hacking station locations cover a lot of nearby sectors. Place them as close to the targets as possible.'

'* There is a tradeoff between efficiency and security. Higher efficiency increases the jump range of your virus but decreases security. Decreased security increases the chances of getting backtracked (victims may try to counter-hack your ships in response).'
'* Advanced Firewall Software protects your ships against counter-hacks. Your big (M6, TM, M8) and huge (all capships) can be counter-hacked.'
'* Expect losses. You may lose additional men after you gain control of the boarded ship. The fewer marines left when the operation completes, the fewer men you will lose.'
'* For tougher targets, make sure to reinforce your marines by sending in more marines.'
'* In general, new marines need to go through 2 decks worth of time in order to reinforce your surviving marines.'
'* Boarding can net you a lot of resources, but it is frowned upon and also has its own set of risks.'
'* Boarding abandoned ships is a good way of training your marines and results in significantly fewer losses than boarded manned ships.'
'* Shield hack and EMP can be used as alternatives to keep your targets shields down.'
'* You get up to the first 25% of a ship blueprint upon successfully boarding that ship. You may gain some money as well.'
'* You can board renegade M6s on Hard Difficulty level. If they were fleeing to a station and they are captured, they may still be over-tuned!'
'* As you progress through the main plot, you can choose to continue helping Phanon or progress through the Synthetic Dawn Plot and join the OCV. Each route has its advantages.'
'* The main plot normally starts when you to have established an empire, but the alternate route can be started as soon as you place your first outpost.'
'* When the Phanon arrive, they will need your help. Speed up their growth by selling shipbuilding materials to them.'
'* Terraforming a planet in one of your sectors will penalize not only the production rates at the local outpost but also at other outposts.'

'* Hacking, ship extensions, and maintenance are free if you join the OCV. You get other benefits, such as improved recruited marines and no food consumption by default. However, this comes at a great cost...'

'* OCV ships are cheaper and stronger than even Terran ships, but any of your OCV ships will eventually turn to OCV control. The time it takes to convert is determined by the abnormal signal strength of the sector they were built (or boarded) in and by ship quality.'

'* Higher abnormal signals and lower ship quality will shorten the timer before OCV ships join the OCV faction. On the plus side, OCV ships are cheaper to build in sectors with higher abnormal signal strength.'
'* Lower abnormal signals and higher ship quality will lengthen the timer before OCV ships join the OCV faction.'
'* Researching OCV ships in a sector with 0% abnormal signal strength is significantly slower than researching OCV ships in a sector with at least 1% abnormal signal strength.'

sval.val: -- Maintenance Tips. Saving Credits ! --
* Avoid deploying any unnecessary Jump Beacons. On the higher difficulty levels, their maintenance cost is very high.
* The "Dry Dock" perk lowers maintenance of docked Capital ships by 75% and smaller ships by 25%.
* Ship Quality directly affects maintenance costs. It can nearly double for the lowest quality ships!
* "Advanced ships" are 35% more expensive to maintain.
* Ships you build that are not of your own Race are higher in maintenance costs.
* For ships produced at outposts having the perk "Advanced engineering", maintenance costs will be cut by 50%.
* Yaki ship maintenance is 25% less while you have infamy.
-- Automated Exploration Tips. --
* Build your own Advanced Satellite Factory and base some fast M5 fighters to it. You can then set them as Automated explorers. This works from outposts also.
* Automated explorers have a 15 jump range from their home base.
* Explorers based at the same station will always explore different sectors without overlap.
* Good to Know: A.I. explorers on hard difficulty level have the ability to claim sectors.
* Explorers will avoid Blacklisted sectors. You may have to explore those personally.
* On Hard difficulty, the other nations will periodically "clean out" some of your satellites, so your automated explorers will stay very busy replacing them.
-- Random Tips. --

* Capital ships do not do very well at docking or traversing through gates when you are in-system with them. They tend to clog up because of their collision avoidance which is active only when you are present in the system. If you want them to move without clogging up, be somewhere else. For moving around within the system, they do ok with you there.

* If you are In System with your fleet, all damage (from all sides) is magnified greatly, so if you want a fight over quickly, be there in that system. Out of system, all damages are reduced to about 1/3.
* Chaff is not considered for OOS battles, so if youre never where the fighting is, dont bother with it. OOS battles are simulated and use a simplified calculation which doesnt consider all factors.
* Upgrade your larger ships in the outpost Hangar, using colored crystals. In particular, the CCDS1/2/3 will allow Chaff to be used to repel the 3 missile types in the game.

* The jump station perk is limited to 4 in the galaxy, so use it in critical areas where you may get attacked and cant risk relying on fragile jump beacons. Losing your jump beacon when trying to respond to an attack will ruin your day.

* Remember you cannot place beacons in sectors you do not own on hard difficulty. This makes expansion far more difficult and mirrors the A.I. limitations. The only means to expand is to use a TL or large Capital ship to move and drop a factory or outpost somewhere and then you can place a beacon.

* The A.I. will sometimes send in small Raiding strikes deep into your territory during war time. These are small fleets of fast fighters that will kill your outpost agents and traders, so protect the homeland.
-- Research Tips. --
* The "Faster research" Perk can greatly improve any research in that sector.
* Researching ships of your own Race gives a large bonus.
* Researching ships of a type matching nations that border that sector gives you a bonus.
* A Research Favor from another race can improve your research rate temporarily.
* If you are in a Coalition, this can improve your research rate.
* OCV ship research is improved in systems that have higher OCV signals.
* Yaki ship research is improved if you have Infamy.
* Terran ships can be researched only in systems that have Terran Memory.
* You can use your data scanner to scan your own ships that you do not have a blueprint of.
-- Fleet Combat Tips. --

* If you cannot catch someone, you cannot kill them. Speed kills. The Split have the fastest ships, but they are somewhat weak in defenses. Used properly, they can be deadly. Each race has their own particular advantages to learn and take advantage of.
* Escort your large Capital ships with some M6s. These provide good anti-fighter defense and they can hold up in a heavy fight.

* Create fast Raiding fleets of M3s and using the Fleet settings screen, set them to attack only Haulers and then set them to patrol an Enemy factions space. They will quickly decimate enemy haulers while running from other fights. This can devastate the economy of an opponent.

* Missiles in Renegades have greatly enhanced damage. They are expensive, but much more damaging than in any prior versions of X3 mods. M7Ms are very effective long range anti-capital forces, and M8s can be devastating against fighters.

* Grouping your forces is essential to surviving large engagements. Streaming in your attack ships 1 by 1 is the best way to lose them. When invading a sector, consider first sending in one or two fast fighters and directing them to the far side of the target system. When the defenses move far from your gate to engage those fighters, stream in your large ships.

* For large capital ship engagements In-System, use fast nimble fighters to draw fire from enemy capital ships and away from your capital ships. These force the enemy to waste their high-damage weapons on nimble hard-to-hit ships.
* Be sure to setup a Supplier in the Fleet Settings screen to automatically restore your missile reserves.
* Moving Capital ships through gates is vastly slower with the player In-System. If you need to get them through a gate fast, be somewhere else.
-- Logistics. --

* In systems where you have no jump beacon, use ONLY your local logistics agents to import/export everything from/to the local factories and then set other logistics agents to move FULL loads between other outposts. This maximizes the inter-sector Loads you carry and is the KEY to efficiency.

* Setup correctly, In most system, you should only need 2 Logistics agents to service all the factories there. For large systems holding 15 factories, you might need 3 agents max, but more is a waste.

* Outpost Trade agents are used for buying materals from NPCs or selling excess items to NPCs. When neither is needed, they start Trading between NPCs for pure profit, so they can be a huge source of income over time. Also remember that any successful trade to an NPC raises your standings with them and that can be a game changer.
* If you can afford the maintenance costs, research a FAST TS class ship to use as your logistics agents. The faster resources are moved around your empire, the smoother it will run.
* If you find your outpost agents doing nothing most of the time, assign them to do something else. Optimize the use of your agents to keep costs down.

* Review the "Logistics" screen in your personal console. This summarizes the total empire production and consumption, showing you exactly when you need more or less factories. It is critical to review when you get a larger empire.

* The default station trade range in Mayhem 3 is 8 jumps (does not include jump beacons). Your agents will limit themselves to this range. If you raise it, the demand on your CPU can rise dramatically, so keep an eye out for this.

* Your logistics ships will need maintenance once in a while. Be sure to review your Maintenance screen in your Personal console and send them for Inspection occasionally. Otherwise their maintenance will be very high.
-- General Tips. --

* The Truelight Seeker is a souped-up repair ship! Target a friendly and shoot, or use the *Repair command* from the special commands and it will carry out the task automatically. It has 6 repair lasers and can repair large ships in the field.
* Do not undervalue Mining ships. While mining ore and silicon, they also bring in colored Crystals which are good for ship upgrades and valuable resources to sell at trade stations.
* When at war, consider placing a few picket ships out 2 or 3 jumps from your main Hubs. This can be an essential early warning system if you get too busy micromanaging.
* The chances that the A.I. will declare war on you go up if you have Infamy, a bad reputation with them, hold a Dejure sector, or if you have a low "Total Ship Power to System Count ratio".

* On hard difficulty and fighting far from home, consider loading a cheap factory and a Jump Beacon on one of your Capital ships, assuming you have one with the necessary cargo space. In a pinch, you can run to an unclaimed sector, deploy the station and then drop the Jump Beacon, allowing you to escape.
* Generally, the A.I. must share a border with you in order to declare war on you.

* Depending on how much progress you have towards a ship blueprint, recycling a ship will give anywhere between 10-40% of its blueprint, up until 85% (50% for advanced ships). The remaining 15% must be completed by research or via the data scanner.

* Different races have different ship advantages and loadouts. The Split have the fastest ships, Teladi have largest cargo bays, Boron have Ion weapon, Terran have most powerful weapons. Each races has their own disadvantages as well.
* Renegade ships move faster when they start fleeing to a station.
-- Fleet Settings Screen Tips. --
* Fleet members can get dispersed during combat operations. You can peridiodically regroup by issuing the "Followers: Join with Commander" command.

* If you want your fleets to focus their fire on one target at a time, set their Scanning Range to 0 km, and set "Followers engage commanders target" to YES. It can be less efficient, but you will lose fewer ships

* You can assign an automated Missile Supplier that will top up all your ships in the field. Upgrade a TS hauler with a Transporter Device and position it out in space. In the Fleet Settings screen, select "Supplier:" and choose this hauler.

* Suppliers will either retrieve missiles from its homebase, or build more there as needed and automatically stock up your ships. Set your ship restock amounts at the bottom of the "Advanced/Weapons.." menu for that ship.
* This screen shows the slowest ship in the fleet. This is important because a fleet travels at the pace of its slowest member.
* For fast raiding fleets composed of fighters, it is useful to select the option to "Ignore Big and Huge Ships".
* Fleets can automatically reinforce themselves by setting the "Build Followers" menu. This is limited to only one type of ship, but it can be useful for homogeneous fleets.
-- Hacking Tips. --
* Port research takes time and money. A higher research rate will improve your port research time.
* Oxygen and accounting hacks take the longest to complete.
* The "hacking station" perk is required to convert a research station into a hacking station.
* Good hacking station locations cover a lot of nearby sectors. Place them as close to the targets as possible.

* There is a tradeoff between efficiency and security. Higher efficiency increases the jump range of your virus but decreases security. Decreased security increases the chances of getting backtracked (victims may try to counter-hack your ships in response).
* Advanced Firewall Software protects your ships against counter-hacks. Your big (M6, TM, M8) and huge (all capships) can be counter-hacked.
--Boarding Tips. --
* Expect losses. You may lose additional men after you gain control of the boarded ship. The fewer marines left when the operation completes, the fewer men you will lose.
* For tougher targets, make sure to reinforce your marines by sending in more marines.
* In general, new marines need to go through 2 decks worth of time in order to reinforce your surviving marines.
* Boarding can net you a lot of resources, but it is frowned upon and also has its own set of risks.
* Boarding abandoned ships is a good way of training your marines and results in significantly fewer losses than boarded manned ships.
* Shield hack and EMP can be used as alternatives to keep your targets shields down.
* You get up to the first 25% of a ship blueprint upon successfully boarding that ship. You may gain some money as well.
* You can board renegade M6s on Hard Difficulty level. If they were fleeing to a station and they are captured, they may still be over-tuned!
-- Storyline and OCV Tips. --
* As you progress through the main plot, you can choose to continue helping Phanon or progress through the Synthetic Dawn Plot and join the OCV. Each route has its advantages.
* The main plot normally starts when you to have established an empire, but the alternate route can be started as soon as you place your first outpost.
* When the Phanon arrive, they will need your help. Speed up their growth by selling shipbuilding materials to them.
* Terraforming a planet in one of your sectors will penalize not only the production rates at the local outpost but also at other outposts.

* Hacking, ship extensions, and maintenance are free if you join the OCV. You get other benefits, such as improved recruited marines and no food consumption by default. However, this comes at a great cost...

* OCV ships are cheaper and stronger than even Terran ships, but any of your OCV ships will eventually turn to OCV control. The time it takes to convert is determined by the abnormal signal strength of the sector they were built (or boarded) in and by ship quality.

* Higher abnormal signals and lower ship quality will shorten the timer before OCV ships join the OCV faction. On the plus side, OCV ships are cheaper to build in sectors with higher abnormal signal strength.
* Lower abnormal signals and higher ship quality will lengthen the timer before OCV ships join the OCV faction.
* Researching OCV ships in a sector with 0% abnormal signal strength is significantly slower than researching OCV ships in a sector with at least 1% abnormal signal strength.
